To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the deformation and martensitic phase transformation in TRIP steel are strongly influenced by grain size and crystal orientation of each grain.
1) The deformation behavior of the TRIP steel with different grain size is simulated by the crystal plasticity finite element method (CP-FEM) with Voronoi tessellations.
(i) the martensitic transformation behavior in polycrytalline TRIP steels is simulated by a finite element simulation with a Voronoi tessellated polycrystal model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of grain number on the deformation and SIMt behavior of the polcrystalline TRP steel at the crystal scale by means of finite element simulation.
the development of the constitutive formula for the polycrystal TRP steel with the SIMT behavior and the simulation of deformation behavior with a SIMT process in polycrystal.
the development of a computational model of martensitic transformation in TRIP steels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deformation behavior of polycrystaline TRIP steel with different grain size is simulated by a crystal plasticity finite element method with Voronoi tessellations.
the present simulation is a useful tool for the understanding of the deformation behavior with a pattern of martensite in TRIP steels with different grain sizes.
the deformation behavior of polycrystaline TRIP steel is strongly dependent on the grain size, and the deformation behavior with a patterned martensitic phase is more sensitive to the grain size.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the simulation result of polycrystalls with different grain size shows a good agreement with experimental results in the past.
the simulation of the deformation behavior with SIMT of the polycristalline TRIP steels by crystal plasticity FEM with a Voronoi tessellations is successfully performed.
the simulation of the martensitic transformation in TRIP steels by the crystal plasticity finite element analysis (CPFEM) with a cellular automata method is feasible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the patterning of martensitic transformation in polycrystal TRiP steel is dependent on grain size and the deformation related length.
the patterning process of the martensitic phase is observed in polycrystal TRiP steel with the different number of grains and the different initial crystal orientations.
the grain size effect on the deformation and SIMTs behavior is clearly demonstrated in the polycrystal TRiP steel by the cellular automata approach.
